- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecast tends to peak too early and then decay too quickly, missing the sustained upward trend seen in true outcomes.
- Overshoots occur after sharp spikes in history (e.g., after 73.21 or 72.37), leading to overcorrection.
- Model underestimates late-period prices (last 5–10 days) despite strong upward momentum in true outcomes.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes prices revert to prior levels too soon, ignoring persistent upward momentum.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: true prices rise faster than model predicts, especially after mid- to late-period spikes.
- Model fails to capture “late breakout” momentum — true prices often surge in final 5–10 days, while model remains flat or slightly declining.
